## Multiple Mitochondrial Dysfunctions Syndrome 7 (MMDS7)

Multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome-7 (MMDS7) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the glycine cleavage system H protein gene (GCSH) on chromosome 16q23.

### Clinical Presentation

MMDS7 is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by a clinical spectrum ranging from neonatal fatal glycine encephalopathy to an attenuated phenotype of developmental delay, behavioral problems, limited epilepsy, and variable movement problems.

Five unrelated patients with glycine encephalopathy were reported, with symptom onset ranging from day 1 of life to 3 months of age. The severity varies considerably, with some patients presenting with severe manifestations in the neonatal period and others showing milder, more attenuated symptoms.

### Biochemical Features

The condition is biochemically characterized by glycine accumulation in body fluids, including the cerebrospinal fluid, with an elevated cerebrospinal fluid/plasma glycine ratio.

The H protein (GCSH) shuttles the methylamine group of glycine and has a pivotal role in the lipoylation of enzymes involved in cellular energetics such as mitochondrial components of pyruvate dehydrogenase complex and 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complex. # Running ODK commands in this repo

## TL;DR

`src/ontology/run.sh` is the official wrapper, but it ends in `docker run -ti` so it **fails silently in any non-TTY context** (Claude Code, CI, non-interactive shells) with `the input device is not a TTY` and exits without running the command.

If you have a TTY, prefer `run.sh`. If you don't, call docker directly with `-i` only.

## When you have a TTY (interactive terminal)

```bash
cd src/ontology && sh run.sh <command> <args...>
```

Examples:
```bash
sh run.sh make NORM
sh run.sh owltools --use-catalog mondo-edit.obo --obsolete-replace MONDO:A MONDO:B -o -f obo mondo-edit.obo
sh run.sh robot verify --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo --queries ../sparql/qc/general/qc-foo.sparql -O reports/
```

## When you don't have a TTY (Claude Code, CI, scripts)

Symptom: `sh run.sh <anything>` prints `the input device is not a TTY` and exits with no further output, no file changes.

Workaround — invoke docker directly using the same image and mounts as `run.sh`, but with `-i` only:

```bash
docker run --memory=8g \
  -v /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/REPO:/work \
  -w /work/src/ontology \
  -e ROBOT_JAVA_ARGS=-Xmx8G -e JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx8G \
  --rm -i obolibrary/odkfull:<TAG-FROM-RUN.SH> \
  <command> <args...>
```

Where:
- `/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/REPO` = the repo root (the parent of `src/`).
- `<TAG-FROM-RUN.SH>` = whatever tag is set in `IMAGE=` in `src/ontology/run.sh`. **Always read `run.sh` first to look up the current tag** — do not hardcode `v1.6` or any other version.

## Reading the right image tag

Don't memorize the version. The line in `run.sh` is the source of truth:

```bash
grep '^IMAGE=' src/ontology/run.sh
# IMAGE=${IMAGE:-odkfull:v1.6}
```

## Common ODK commands you'll need

| What | Command body (after `run.sh` or after the `docker run ... -i obolibrary/odkfull:<TAG>` prefix) |
|---|---|
| Normalize edit file | `make NORM` then `mv NORM mondo-edit.obo` (run from `src/ontology`) |
| Convert / syntax check | `robot convert --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo -f obo -o mondo-edit.TMP.obo` |
| Run a QC query | `robot verify --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo --queries ../sparql/qc/general/qc-X.sparql -O reports/` |
| Merge / obsolete with replacement | `owltools --use-catalog mondo-edit.obo --obsolete-replace MONDO:A MONDO:B -o -f obo mondo-edit.obo` |

## Notes

- All ODK commands assume CWD is `src/ontology/`.
- `make NORM` writes to a file called `NORM` in `src/ontology/`. You must `mv NORM mondo-edit.obo` afterward.
- `robot verify` exits non-zero on QC failures and writes one TSV per failing query under `-O reports/`. Empty exit + `PASS Rule ... 0 violation(s)` = clean.
- If `run.sh` reports `the input device is not a TTY`, do **not** retry the same command — it will keep failing. Switch to the docker-direct invocation.

## Summary

This PR addresses issue #9896 by renaming MONDO:0957382 from "multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome 7" to "GCSH-related glycine encephalopathy" and reclassifying it under the appropriate parent term.

## Background Research

OMIM:620423 describes an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the GCSH gene (glycine cleavage system H protein). The condition presents a clinical spectrum ranging from neonatal fatal glycine encephalopathy to attenuated phenotypes with developmental delay, behavioral problems, limited epilepsy, and movement problems. Biochemically, it is characterized by glycine accumulation in body fluids and elevated cerebrospinal fluid/plasma glycine ratio.

Despite its previous name suggesting it was primarily a mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome, the literature and clinical presentation clearly indicate this is a form of glycine encephalopathy. The GCSH protein is part of the glycine cleavage system, and its dysfunction results in the same biochemical and clinical features as other forms of glycine encephalopathy.

## Changes Made

### 1. Term Renaming
- **Old name:** multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome 7
- **New name:** GCSH-related glycine encephalopathy
- Follows MONDO's gene-disease naming convention and ClinGen preferred label

### 2. Reparenting
- **Old parent:** MONDO:0017338 (fatal multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome)
- **New parent:** MONDO:0011612 (glycine encephalopathy)
- This aligns with existing gene-specific glycine encephalopathy terms:
  - MONDO:0958179 (glycine encephalopathy 1) - GLDC gene
  - MONDO:0958192 (glycine encephalopathy 2) - AMT gene
  - MONDO:0015010 (atypical glycine encephalopathy) - SLC6A9 gene

### 3. Definition Added
Following the disease_series_by_gene pattern, added a comprehensive definition that includes:
- The genetic basis (variation in GCSH gene)
- Clinical spectrum description
- Biochemical features
- Proper citations [MONDO:patterns/disease_series_by_gene, OMIM:620423]

### 4. Synonyms Added
- "GCSH glycine encephalopathy" [OMIM:620423]
- "GCSH-related glycine encephalopathy" with ClinGen preferred label qualifier
- "glycine encephalopathy caused by variation in GCSH" [MONDO:patterns/disease_series_by_gene]
- "MMDS7" (abbreviation) [OMIM:620423]

Added intersection_of axioms following the disease_series_by_gene pattern:
- intersection_of: MONDO:0011612 (glycine encephalopathy)
- intersection_of: has_material_basis_in_germline_mutation_in http://identifiers.org/hgnc/4208 (GCSH)

### 6. Metadata
- Added excluded_subClassOf relationship documenting removal of previous parent (MONDO:0017338)
- Added clingen subset
- Added creator attribution (ORCID: 0000-0002-7437-8060)
- Added issue tracker reference (IAO:0000233)

✅ Normalization completed successfully using ODK make NORM
✅ Term structure follows disease_series_by_gene pattern
✅ All synonyms properly cited
✅ ClinGen preferred label included with proper qualifier

## Rationale

The reparenting decision was based on:
1. The molecular mechanism - GCSH is part of the glycine cleavage system
2. The biochemical phenotype - glycine accumulation is the primary feature
3. The clinical presentation - overlaps with other forms of glycine encephalopathy
4. Consistency with existing MONDO structure - other gene-specific glycine encephalopathy terms are children of MONDO:0011612
5. ClinGen's preferred label suggesting the primary classification should be as glycine encephalopathy

The term "multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome" appears to have been based on the secondary effects of GCSH dysfunction on mitochondrial lipoylation, but the primary disease mechanism and phenotype is glycine encephalopathy.
